chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalesi, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awn narrated from Ibn Abi Najran al-Tamimi, who said: 'Asim ibn Hamit al-Hannat narrated from Abi Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Three [types of people] to whom God will not speak on the Day of Resurrection, nor look at them, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: The one who plucks his white hair (beard), the one who masturbates, and the one who is penetrated anally.

key_terms.النَّاتِفُ شَيْبَهُ: The one who plucks his white hair (beard)
key_terms.وَالْمَنْكُوحُ فِي دُبُرِهِ: The one who is penetrated anally
key_terms.وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ: And for them is a painful punishment

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people God will not speak to on the Day of Judgment according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three categories as distinct manifestations of physical and spiritual impurity, linking bodily neglect to divine rejection. The 'Natthaf' (one who plucks white beard hairs) is often interpreted by Shia scholars as a symbol of vanity or altering God's creation, while the other two represent specific sexual transgressions. This triad underscores the holistic nature of accountability in Shia jurisprudence, where physical acts carry profound eschatological weight.
